title: Using tab in inspector triggers tool setter twice
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.6.stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS 24.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon 760M (radeonsi, phoenix, LLVM 20.1.2, DRM 3.57, 6.8.0-90-generic) - AMD Ryzen 5 7640U w/ Radeon 760M Graphics (12 threads) - 13.45 GiB memory

### Issue description

In a tool, export Variables with multiple values (e.g. `Vector2`) can trigger the setter more than once even if only one value was changed.
This is a problem in my case. My actual setter updates both values the first time but rejects the second change, which results in the same value(s) as before the setter was triggered twice. The MRP does not have this problem but solving the double trigger would also solve my issue.

More generally speaking, this always occurs when a setter is trying to update another value that you tab into in the inspector. (Tested with `Vector3`)

Setters also seem to have an inconsistent problem with onready variables, sometimes complaining that the type is 'Nil' when loading the project. Might open another issue for that later, unless it's already known?

Edit: The inspector should also update the value correctly (after a fix), so I guess there are possible two different root causes at work here.

### Steps to reproduce

- write a setter for a variable with multiple values (e.g. `Vector2`) in a tool script
- optional: include a `print()` line for better clarity
- change one of the values in the variable, except the last one
- press tab => setter is triggered and the following, now selected value is not updated (probably uses some cache that is updated too late?)
- press tab again => setter is triggered again, since the value was not updated in the previous step

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[setter-multi-trigger.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24893351/setter-multi-trigger.zip)
